scenarios.title: 'Can You Win the League?'
scenarios.text: Pre-match press conference. A journalist from {OUT} asks the question everyone wants answered: 'Can {club} win the league this season?' The cameras zoom in.
scenarios.prompt: What do you say?

choices.label: 'Yes. Why not us?'
choices.hint: Fans love it. Rivals print it.
choices.text: The quote is everywhere. The fans make it a banner. The rival's dressing room pins it on their wall.

choices.label: 'One game at a time.'
choices.text: The journalists sigh. The manager nods approvingly.

choices.label: 'Ask me in May.'
choices.text: The room laughs. The clip is shared as 'the most confident non-answer of the season'.

scenarios.title: The Pundit
text: A famous TV pundit, a former international, has said on air that {J} 'will never be good enough for the top level'. He's said it three weeks running.
A pundit spends six minutes of prime-time TV dissecting one bad touch from {J}'s last match, with arrows, circles and a slow-motion replay.
scenarios.prompt: A TV pundit keeps tearing into you.

choices.label: Ignore him and keep playing
choices.text: He says nothing. After his next good game, the pundit grudgingly admits he 'might have been a bit harsh'.

out.text: The pundit comes. He's surprisingly humble. The resulting TV segment changes how the country sees {J}.
The pundit declines on air: 'I don't need to watch him train. I've watched him play.'

choices.label: Fire back on social media
choices.desc: Remind him of his own career.
choices.text: He posts the pundit's own worst miss. Millions laugh. The pundit makes it his mission to criticise {J} forever.

scenarios.title: A Political Question
scenarios.text: At a press conference, a reporter asks about a controversial political issue in the country. It has nothing to do with football. Every answer will anger somebody.
scenarios.prompt: A political question at a football press conference.

choices.label: 'I'm here to talk about football.'
choices.text: He politely declines. Some say he's dodging. Most say he's sensible.

choices.label: Give a careful, human answer
choices.text: His answer is thoughtful and kind. It's praised by many and twisted by some.

scenarios.title: Linked
text: This week's transfer gossip column links {J} with four clubs in three countries. His agent has spoken to none of them.
A foreign newspaper claims {J} has been 'scouted extensively' by a club he's never heard of. His mother has already started learning the language.
scenarios.prompt: The transfer rumours are everywhere.

choices.label: Ignore them
choices.text: He ignores them. The rumours fade by Thursday and new ones arrive by Friday.

choices.label: Kiss the badge after your next goal
choices.text: He scores and kisses the badge. The fans go wild. The rumours become 'loyalty' stories.

choices.label: Tell your agent to use the interest
choices.text: His agent uses the noise. The club offers talks about a new deal.

scenarios.title: Out of Context
scenarios.text: A clip of {J} laughing during a minute's silence is going viral. He wasn't laughing: he was coughing. The video doesn't have sound. Nobody cares about the sound.
scenarios.prompt: A misleading clip is spreading.

choices.label: Post the full footage with sound
choices.text: The full clip shows him coughing into his elbow. The storm turns into apologies within a day.

choices.label: Apologise anyway
choices.text: His apology makes people think he really did laugh. The storm doubles.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.text: It blows over in a week. Some people still believe it.

scenarios.title: On Camera
scenarios.text: In a post-match interview, the reporter asks about his family and his voice cracks. He's on live TV, close to tears, and the reporter is holding the microphone a little closer.
scenarios.prompt: You're about to cry on live TV.

choices.label: Let it happen
choices.text: He lets the tears come and says how much he misses home. The clip moves the whole country. Strangers send letters.

choices.label: Pull yourself together and walk off
choices.text: He says 'excuse me' and walks off. The reporter looks guilty. People respect the dignity.

scenarios.title: The Other Manager's Words
scenarios.text: {R}'s manager says in his press conference that {J} 'dives more than he dribbles'. Now every reporter wants {J}'s reaction.
scenarios.prompt: A rival manager insulted you.

choices.label: 'I'll let him enjoy his opinion.'
choices.text: The calm reply makes the rival manager look petty. The fans love it.

choices.label: 'He should worry about his own team.'
choices.text: The headline writes itself. The match next month sells out in an hour.

scenarios.title: The Top 100
scenarios.text: A football magazine publishes its list of the world's top 100 players. {J} is on it, at number 94. His teammate is at 71. His rival is at 63.
scenarios.prompt: You made the world's top 100 list, low down.

choices.label: Celebrate it
choices.text: He posts it with genuine joy. 'Ninety-four in the world. My mum is ranking me number one.' It's adorable.

choices.label: Use it as fuel
choices.text: He screenshots the list and puts it on his wall. Next year's list will be different.

scenarios.title: The Voice Note
scenarios.text: A private voice note of {J} complaining about the club's medical staff has leaked. Someone he trusted forwarded it. It's playing on every sports show in the country.
scenarios.prompt: A private voice note has leaked.

choices.label: Apologise to the medical staff in person
choices.text: He goes to the medical department with coffee and an honest apology. They accept. Some of what he said was fair, and they know it.

choices.label: Stand by what you said
choices.text: He stands by it. The board is livid. The medical staff, quietly, start doing things differently.

scenarios.title: Snubbed
scenarios.text: The league's team of the season is announced. He isn't in it. A player with worse numbers in every category is. The fans are outraged on his behalf.
scenarios.prompt: You were left out of the team of the season.

choices.label: Congratulate the winners publicly
choices.text: His gracious post makes the snub look even worse. The fans love him for it.

choices.label: Let your numbers speak
choices.text: He posts his stats with no caption. It's the most-liked post of his career.

scenarios.title: Fan TV
scenarios.text: A popular fan TV channel films angry supporters outside the stadium after every match. One of them has a catchphrase about {J} that's become a meme. It is not affectionate.
scenarios.prompt: A fan TV channel has made you a meme.

out.text: He turns up unannounced. The angry fan is lost for words, then hugs him. The video is the channel's biggest ever.
The fan doesn't back down and it turns into an argument on camera. Awkward.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.text: He ignores it. The meme fades when he scores twice.

scenarios.title: Who?
scenarios.text: An international broadcaster calls him by a teammate's name for the whole of a live match. Social media in his country is furious on his behalf.
scenarios.prompt: A broadcaster got your name wrong for ninety minutes.

choices.label: Joke about it
choices.desc: Change your profile name for a day.
choices.text: He changes his name online to the wrong one for twenty-four hours. The broadcaster apologises on air. Everyone laughs.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.text: He lets it go and promises himself the world will learn his name.

scenarios.title: The Old Club's Documentary
scenarios.text: His first club, {FIRSTCLUB}, is making a documentary about its history. They want to interview him about where it all began. The old president, who once told him he'd never make it, is in it too.
scenarios.prompt: Take part in your first club's documentary?

choices.label: Yes, warmly
choices.text: He talks for an hour about the club that made him. The old president, it turns out, cries when he watches it.

choices.label: Yes, and tell the truth about the hard times
choices.text: He talks about the unpaid wages and the cold showers. The documentary is better for it. Some old directors aren't happy.

scenarios.title: 1:47am
scenarios.text: 1:47am. He's typed a long post about how nobody appreciates what players go through. His thumb is hovering over 'post'.
scenarios.prompt: Post the late-night rant?

out.text: Strangely, it resonates. Other players share it. A conversation about mental health starts.
It reads as self-pity from a millionaire. The replies are brutal.

choices.label: Delete it and go to sleep
choices.text: He deletes it and sleeps. In the morning he's very glad.

choices.label: Send it to {BFf} instead
choices.text: {BFf} replies in two minutes: 'Bro. Go to sleep. I'm proud of you.'

scenarios.title: The Favour
scenarios.text: {JR}, who has always written kindly about him, asks a favour: the inside story on a dressing-room row. Just a hint. 'You know I'll protect you.'
scenarios.prompt: A friendly journalist wants inside information.

choices.label: Politely refuse
choices.text: He refuses. {JRl} smiles and says he understands. The next piece is a little less warm.

choices.label: Give him a harmless detail
choices.text: He gives a harmless detail. It isn't harmless once it's in print.

scenarios.title: The Toughest Interview
scenarios.text: A children's TV show sends three eight-year-olds to interview him. Their questions: 'Do you cry when you lose?', 'Who's your best friend?', and 'Why is your hair like that?'
scenarios.prompt: How do you handle the kids' interview?

choices.label: Answer everything honestly
choices.text: 'Yes, I cry when I lose. My best friend is called {BFf}. My hair is a mistake.' The clip is the cutest thing on the internet for a week.

choices.label: Turn it round and interview them
choices.text: He interviews them instead. One of them wants to be a goalkeeper and an astronaut. Lovely.

scenarios.title: Walk Past or Stop?
scenarios.text: After a humiliating defeat, the mixed zone is full of microphones. The press officer says he can walk past if he wants. The journalists are watching to see who stops.
scenarios.prompt: Talk to the media after a heavy defeat?

choices.label: Stop and take responsibility
choices.text: He stops and says it plainly: 'We were not good enough. I was not good enough.' The journalists write that he was the only one who stopped.

choices.label: Walk past
choices.text: He walks past with his headphones on. 'Hiding,' says one column.

scenarios.title: What {T} Said
scenarios.text: {T} went on a podcast and, asked about {J}, said: 'Talented, but he needs to grow up.' The clip has two million views.
scenarios.prompt: A teammate criticised you on a podcast.

out.text: {T} says it was clipped out of context; he'd also called {J} the best young player he'd seen. They post a photo together. Done.
{T} says he meant every word. At least it's honest.

choices.label: Reply publicly
choices.text: His reply starts a public feud. The manager has to separate them in training.

scenarios.title: The Sponsor's Post
scenarios.text: One of his sponsors posted a picture of him with a caption written in his voice: 'Best weekend ever!' He didn't write it. It went out an hour after his team lost 4-0.
scenarios.prompt: A sponsor posted badly-timed content in your name.

choices.label: Ask them to delete it, and say so
choices.text: He asks them to delete it and explains that he didn't write it. The fans forgive him. The sponsor's social media manager is having a terrible day.

choices.label: Let it go quietly
choices.text: The fans blame him. The sponsor never realises the damage.

scenarios.title: Half-Time Interview
scenarios.text: Walking off at half-time, 0-2 down, a pitchside reporter sticks a microphone in his face: 'What's going wrong out there?'
scenarios.prompt: A half-time microphone.

choices.label: 'We'll fix it.'
choices.text: Three words, then the tunnel. Nothing to see.

choices.label: Say exactly what's going wrong
choices.text: 'Nobody is running.' Live on TV. The manager hears it in the dressing room before {J} gets there.

scenarios.title: 'The Next Big Thing'
scenarios.text: A big columnist writes a whole page about {J}: 'the next big thing', 'a generational talent'. Strangers recognise him in the street for the first time. The squad will never let him forget the word 'generational'.
scenarios.prompt: The media is hyping you up.

choices.label: Keep your feet on the ground
choices.text: He shrugs it off in training and works harder. The squad calls him 'Generational' anyway, affectionately.

choices.label: Enjoy it
choices.text: He enjoys the attention. A little too much. A senior player has a quiet word.

scenarios.title: 'When Will You Retire?'
scenarios.text: Every press conference now ends with the same question: when will he retire? He's playing well. They keep asking anyway.
scenarios.prompt: The retirement question, again.

choices.label: 'When my legs tell me.'
choices.text: His calm answer stops the question for a month. A record.

choices.label: 'Ask my last opponent.'
choices.text: The quote goes on a T-shirt. The fans buy thousands.

scenarios.title: The Photographer
scenarios.text: An old pitchside photographer, who has taken pictures of {J} since his first match, is retiring. He's sent {J} a box of prints: every important moment of his career, from the stands.
scenarios.prompt: An old photographer sends you your whole career in pictures.

choices.label: Visit him to say thank you
choices.text: He visits with a signed shirt. The old man tells him stories about every photo. They're the best stories {J} has ever heard about himself.

choices.label: Fund an exhibition of his work
choices.text: The exhibition opens in the city centre. The photographer stands in front of his own work and cries.

scenarios.title: The Accusation
scenarios.text: An influencer claims {J} was rude to her at a restaurant. He has never met her. The restaurant's cameras show he was across the city that night.
scenarios.prompt: A false accusation from an influencer.

choices.label: Release the evidence calmly
choices.text: He shares the evidence calmly. The influencer deletes her post and apologises. His calm wins.

choices.label: Sue for defamation
choices.text: The lawsuit settles quickly. The money goes to charity. Nobody accuses him of anything for a while.

scenarios.title: The Kit Leak
scenarios.text: He accidentally posts a photo with next season's kit visible in the background. The kit manufacturer had planned a big launch. The internet has already decided the kit is ugly.
scenarios.prompt: You leaked the new kit.

choices.label: Apologise to the club and the brand
choices.text: He apologises. The brand turns it into a 'leaked by {J}' campaign. It's their best-selling kit in years.

choices.label: Pretend it's an old photo
choices.text: Nobody believes it. The club fines him a symbolic amount.

scenarios.title: 'Why Won't He Talk?'
scenarios.text: He hasn't given an interview in months. The press have started writing about his silence: 'arrogant', 'hiding', 'too big for us now'.
scenarios.prompt: The press resent your silence.

choices.label: Give one long, honest interview
choices.desc: End the silence on your terms.
choices.text: One long interview, with the journalist he trusts most. It's warm and honest. The 'arrogant' stories stop.

choices.label: Keep your silence
choices.text: He stays silent. The press stays hostile. The fans don't mind.

scenarios.title: Mail
scenarios.text: The club's mailroom has a whole shelf for him: drawings, letters, requests for shirts, a marriage proposal from a seventy-year-old woman, a letter from a prisoner.
scenarios.prompt: A mountain of fan mail.

choices.label: Reply to ten letters a week, by hand
choices.hint: Some people will keep your letter forever.
choices.text: Ten letters a week, by hand. One reply goes to a boy in hospital. His mother posts it online. It's shared a million times.

choices.label: Let the club handle it
choices.text: Signed photos go out to everyone. Efficient, kind enough.

scenarios.title: In Their Language
scenarios.text: His first press conference in the local language. He's practised for weeks. The translator is sitting next to him, just in case.
scenarios.prompt: Speak the local language at the press conference?

choices.label: Do it all in their language

out.text: He makes eight mistakes and gets a round of applause. The local fans adore him from that day on.
He accidentally says something very rude instead of 'thank you'. The room explodes with laughter. It becomes a beloved story.

choices.label: Use the translator
choices.text: Precise, careful answers through the translator. Fine.

scenarios.title: The Mascot
scenarios.text: The match mascot, a seven-year-old girl, is so nervous she freezes in the tunnel. Thirty thousand people are waiting. {J} is standing next to her.
scenarios.prompt: The mascot is frozen with fear.

choices.label: Carry her out on your shoulders
choices.text: He lifts her on his shoulders and walks out like it's a parade. She waves at the crowd. The photo is the image of the season.

choices.label: Kneel down and talk to her
choices.text: He kneels and tells her he's scared too. She giggles and walks out holding his hand.

scenarios.title: The Thread
scenarios.text: A data analyst posts a forty-tweet thread proving, with charts, that {J} is either massively underrated or massively overrated, depending on which half you read.
scenarios.prompt: A viral data thread about you.

choices.label: Reply: 'Can you send this to my agent?'
choices.text: His reply gets more likes than the thread. The analyst becomes a fan for life.

choices.label: Actually read it
choices.text: He reads all forty tweets. Tweet twenty-seven teaches him something real about his positioning.
